question: In the DX-Scorecard MBR Reviews entry screen, if a draft for the next month already exists on disk (in-progress, not yet locked), should its start card still show "Pull data & start" (re-pulling/reseeding) or a "Continue draft" affordance, and does re-pulling an in-progress draft preserve existing insights and manual values per the re-pull-preservation rule?
recommendation: When an in-progress (unlocked) draft already exists on disk, the start card should present a "Continue draft" affordance that resumes the existing draft in place — NOT a "Pull data & start" reseed. Re-pulling should never be the default entry action for an existing draft; a fresh reseed must be a separate, explicitly confirmed 'discard' action. And yes: a re-pull performed on an in-progress draft preserves existing human insights and manual (unwired) values per the re-pull-preservation rule — only wired KPIs get fresh source values, everything else carries forward. A full reseed/discard is the one path that overwrites them.
supporting_points: MbrBuilderView already encodes exactly this intent: its header comment states "'New MBR' RESUMES an existing on-disk draft rather than overwriting it; a fresh re-seed of the draft happens only after an explicit, confirmed discard," and handleNewMbr() resumes onDiskDraft when present ("Resumed the existing on-disk draft") and only calls seedFresh() when there is nothing on disk — so the entry affordance for an existing draft is Continue/Resume, not Pull-&-start.

The re-pull-preservation rule holds for a targeted re-pull: 'Refresh all data'/per-KPI Refresh only refreshes WIRED KPIs (WIRED_METRIC_IDS), while seededCarried() keeps unwired KPIs' carried values, and editKpi persists status/insight edits — so insights and manual (unwired) values survive a re-pull. reconcileRoster likewise carries value/status/insight forward for every matched KPI, clearing only genuinely-new roster KPIs.

The ONLY destructive path is an explicit, confirmed reseed: seedFresh() is reached solely via the 'Discard draft' modal, whose copy warns it "overwrites the on-disk draft and cannot be undone (use git to recover)." Making "Pull data & start" the start-card affordance for an existing draft would silently invoke that overwrite path and violate the preservation rule, so the start card must instead offer Continue draft and keep reseed behind a guarded Discard.
